children: Spain's manufacturing activity slipped back into contraction in August as output and new orders declined amid stagnant demand and rising energy prices, a business survey showed on Tuesday.
The S&P Spain Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index fell to 49.5 in August from 50.2 in July. The 50 mark separates growth from contraction.

"August proved to be a somewhat challenging month for Spain's manufacturing sector, with output and new orders declining on the month amid stagnant market demand," said Paul Smith, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Output fell for a third straight month and at the sharpest pace since December 2023. New orders declined for a fourth consecutive month, with domestic and international sales both falling, although the drop in export orders was only marginal.

Manufacturers cut jobs for a 12th successive month, and the pace of decline accelerated to its fastest since April. Firms also reduced purchasing activity for a ninth month, with the contraction the steepest since April 2025.

Input cost inflation accelerated noticeably, driven mainly by higher energy prices as well as by transport and raw material costs. Companies raised output prices, too, but the increase remained much weaker than the rise in input costs.
